corrected_answer:
Analytical stance under test: Stance 120 - Host-side NUMA and PCIe placement is a hidden third topology that can dominate whichever parallel axis is chosen.

Common frame (applies to every stance below).
Assumptions (must be restated by the answering engineer, not inherited silently):
A1. Single node, 8 GPUs, NVLink/NVSwitch intra-node; inter-node paths only appear where a stance says so explicitly.
A2. Decode-dominant, latency-sensitive serving: the SLO is TTFT p95 and TPOT (inter-token latency) p95, never a mean.
A3. Model weights fit in aggregate HBM with at least 20% KV-cache headroom at target concurrency.
A4. Exactly one variable moves per arm: no simultaneous change of quantization, batching policy, or speculative decoding.
Mechanism, stated plainly:
- Tensor parallelism (TP) shards every layer's GEMMs. Each transformer block needs two all-reduces (after attention out-projection and after the MLP down-projection), so decode carries L * 2 * allreduce_latency of synchronous cost, where L is the layer count. TP is latency-additive in collectives but capacity- and bandwidth-multiplying: per-GPU weight bytes and per-GPU KV bytes both fall by the TP degree.
- Pipeline parallelism (PP) shards layers into stages. Per token it adds only (PP-1) small point-to-point hidden-state sends, which are cheap, but a single request serializes through all stages and the bubble fraction is (PP-1)/(micro_batches + PP-1). At low concurrency there are too few in-flight micro-batches to fill the pipeline, so PP loses badly on single-request latency.
Boundary conditions that flip the answer:
- B1. On NVLink-class fabric, small-message all-reduce latency is in the single-digit microseconds and TP up to 8 is normally latency-viable. Over PCIe-only or across nodes on RoCE/IB the same collective's latency floor rises roughly an order of magnitude and TP stops paying past TP=2 (ESTIMATE; derivation: decode all-reduce payload is hidden_size * dtype_bytes per token per layer, which is small, so the collective is latency-bound rather than bandwidth-bound and the per-hop latency floor dominates).
- B2. If the model cannot fit on one GPU, sharding is mandatory and the question reduces to which axis, not whether.
- B3. Under high, steady concurrency the PP bubble amortizes and PP becomes competitive on throughput per GPU while still losing on single-request latency.
Default recommendation: use TP inside the node up to the point where collective cost stops being repaid by reduced per-GPU memory traffic; use PP only to cross a node boundary or to fit a model TP alone cannot fit. PP is not a latency optimization.

Only values read out of named benchmark artifacts may be labelled MEASURED. This review reports no MEASURED values, because no benchmark was executed for it.

Neither TP nor PP runs purely on the accelerator fabric. Sampling, detokenisation, request marshalling, and any KV offload or spilling cross the host bus, and on a dual-socket box the GPU-to-socket affinity decides whether those transfers traverse the inter-socket link. A layout that spreads a replica across GPUs hanging off both root complexes pays host-path cost that a socket-local layout does not, and this cost appears in the same latency number that the parallelism argument is trying to explain. Falsifiable hypothesis H120: pinning every rank of a replica to GPUs and CPU cores under a single NUMA node will shift the measured TP-versus-PP gap by an amount comparable to the gap itself on a dual-socket host, so any comparison run without declared affinity is unattributable (ESTIMATE; derivation: inter-socket hops add host-memory latency and reduce effective host-to-device bandwidth relative to a socket-local path, and decode issues many small host-side operations per token, so the per-token host overhead is multiplied by output length). Controlled experiment: Run each arm twice, once with explicit NUMA-local pinning of ranks, worker threads and pinned host buffers, and once with the scheduler's default placement, holding model, engine, quantisation and scheduler settings fixed. Report the four cells, not two. Rollback gate: revert to the previously validated layout if the canary's TTFT p95, TPOT p95 or error rate breaches the pre-declared bound, regardless of any aggregate throughput gain observed.

A parallel layout is not a runtime flag with no history: weights must be materialised in the shard layout the engine expects, and changing tensor degree changes how every weight matrix is split, which changes load time, page-cache behaviour and, if a conversion step exists, the artifact stored on disk. Pipeline degree instead changes which layers land on which device, which is usually cheaper to re-shard but changes the per-stage load skew. Restart and rollback time is an availability term, and it is set by exactly this cost. Falsifiable hypothesis H121: cold-start time to first served token will differ measurably between the two arms even when steady-state latency does not, and the arm with the larger tensor degree will show the larger sensitivity to whether weights are served from page cache or from cold storage (ESTIMATE; derivation: higher tensor degree means more, smaller per-rank weight files and more concurrent readers against the same storage path, so the load stage is more sensitive to storage concurrency behaviour than to total bytes). Controlled experiment: Measure cold start three times per arm from a dropped page cache, and three times warm, recording time to model-loaded and time to first successfully served request separately, with storage backend and file layout identical across arms. Rollback gate: revert to the previously validated layout if the canary's TTFT p95, TPOT p95 or error rate breaches the pre-declared bound, regardless of any aggregate throughput gain observed.

Changing the shard axis changes reduction order, kernel selection and sometimes the sampling code path. Downstream consumers may depend on token-level streaming granularity, logprob values, stop-sequence handling or deterministic output under a fixed seed. If arm B is faster but returns different logprobs or chunks tokens differently, the comparison is between two different services, and the latency winner may be unshippable regardless of its number. Falsifiable hypothesis H122: with temperature zero and a fixed seed, the two arms will produce token sequences that agree on the overwhelming majority of prompts but will diverge on a non-trivial minority, and the divergence rate will grow with output length (ESTIMATE; derivation: floating-point reduction order differs between shard layouts, producing small logit differences that are usually below the argmax margin but occasionally cross it, and each generated token is another independent opportunity to cross). Controlled experiment: Replay a fixed prompt set of at least several hundred prompts through both arms at temperature zero with a fixed seed, and diff outputs token by token, reporting exact-match rate, first-divergence position distribution, and maximum absolute logprob difference. Only then compare latency. Rollback gate: revert to the previously validated layout if the canary's TTFT p95, TPOT p95 or error rate breaches the pre-declared bound, regardless of any aggregate throughput gain observed.

If the service hosts a base model plus many low-rank adapters, per-GPU memory is not just weights plus KV: it is weights, KV, and a resident adapter pool whose size scales with tenant count. Tensor parallelism divides base weights and KV across ranks but adapter application adds per-request small GEMMs whose cost is poorly amortised at low batch, and adapter swap traffic crosses the host bus. Pipeline parallelism instead concentrates each adapter's layers on the stage that owns them, which changes the swap pattern entirely. Controlled experiment: Sweep resident adapter count across at least three levels, from one to production cardinality, on both arms with identical adapter ranks and identical routing traffic, and report the gap per level along with adapter eviction counts. Rollback gate: revert to the previously validated layout if the canary's TTFT p95, TPOT p95 or error rate breaches the pre-declared bound, regardless of any aggregate throughput gain observed.
